A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DoPR research work, with complete, readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A. Pages 3–13 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; differences are confined to attribution and layout on pages 1–2.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning experiments, including benchmark comparisons, training-data and rollout-budget studies, ablations, and runtime measurements in Tables 1–4 and Figures 1 and 3.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 1 and 3.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain identical reward-statistics updates, EM-UCB acquisition scores, single-instance selection, rollout allocation, and GRPO policy updates.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DeepScaleR-Preview training data and evaluate AIME24, AMC, MATH, Minerva Math, OlympiadBench, and GSM8K. No dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 1 retains the base models, GRPO, One-Shot RL, and UFO; Table 3 retains GRPO and One-Shot RL as comparators to DoPR.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Tables 2–3 retain the same model configurations, Pass@1 metric, training-step specification, sample sizes, and rollout-budget settings. No evaluation procedure is revised.

E4.justification: The training-data-scale analysis, DoPR-UCB and DoPR-None ablations, and response-length and update-time analyses are identical in both versions.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or random seeds, or reports confidence intervals or significance tests for the experiments.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4, curves in Figures 1 and 3, and reported experimental findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports the same 49.6 average Pass@1 for DoPR Qwen 1.5B in both versions.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1, its assumptions and derivation, and the detailed proof in Appendix A are identical. No mathematical definition, assumption, or proof is revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about sample complexity, reasoning performance with few training examples, and reduced rollout costs through DoPR.

C2.justification: Interpretations of RL as activating existing capabilities, degradation with eight training samples, and EM-UCB's efficiency benefits are unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the experimental settings provide identical technical and reproducibility information. There are no added or revised implementation details, hardware disclosures, hyperparameter values, or code/data access instructions.

R1.justification: The cited works, Section 2's related-work discussion, and the claimed positioning against earlier RLVR and data-selection approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds equal-contribution markers for Yunjian Zhang and Sudong Wang and an accompanying footnote, changes Yao Zhu's corresponding-author marker, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The additional attribution footnote causes limited column and page reflow and spacing changes on pages 1–2. Figures 1–3, Tables 1–4, Algorithm 1, and the layout of pages 3–13 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies equal-contribution credit and introduces minor layout reflow. The scientific content, experimental evidence, theoretical arguments, and reproducibility information—including Appendix A—remain identical, establishing no meaningful change in overall research quality.
